meta.face: Paul as on the paul card, a little younger (about forty-five): a noble, kindly LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with a receding hairline and dark wavy hair at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes now wide with awe, a long dark pointed beard reaching well below the chin. The companions: small, one a young man with a round face and short black hair, the other older with a grey short beard, both faces half-turned away.
meta.basis: Paul keeps the face of the existing paul card (bald crown, dark wavy side hair, long dark pointed beard), the Byzantine type from the Painter's Manual. The scene follows Acts 9:3-7 and the Western tradition of the fall from the horse, as in Caravaggio's Conversion on the Way to Damascus.
